findings.text: the fragment states '1 failed, 4 passed, EXIT=1' for the reader control and '2 failed, 3 passed, EXIT=1' for the writer control, but negative-control-reader.log contains only 'F....' with no pytest summary or exit line and negative-control-writer.log ends at its summary with no exit line; the manifest's negative_control_log names the writer log, so a promotion reading exit status from that log finds none. The repair is a re-run of both controls with a bare EXIT= last line, not a code change.

_mounted_projects swallows every exception into () and _run_record_held (:1742) into False, and the delta makes that empty tuple authoritative for a whole list at :1820, so an unreadable mount registry is indistinguishable from a registry naming no projects; the reader then records a wait-unresolvable duty whose next_command at obligations.py:1818 advises discarding the request.

dispatch_waits calls _mounted_projects() unconditionally, unlike wait_projects_for at :1820 which guards on a run ref being present, so every dispatch pays a config-home registry read even when no wait names a run.

the mounted-project scan forks runs._promoted_record_project (reckon/crew/runs.py:1783, used at reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py:78) which already searches each mounted project's ledger for a run's row, and it resolves the ledger through the default root while the owner resolves it through each mounted checkout; the fork predates this delta (already reviewed at ce0f36c449) and the delta deepens its reach.
